objectives.text: Attack RFC 0011, the plan and the implementing brief as an opponent would: run a pre-mortem (assume the implementation failed in use and list why), argue the strongest case for the rejected option of every point the RFC settles itself (section 4), and find what is wrong, missing, ambiguous or unsafe: concurrency and locking, worktree isolation, SessionEnd timing, cross-platform, security and privacy (the aitools repo is open-source), migration and data loss, and every sentence an implementer could read two ways.
objectives.how: Read the three targets, the code they rest on (harness-db.py, ait-harvest.py, the SessionStart/SessionEnd hooks, intelligence-stop.py, deploy-harness.sh), the harvest log, git history and repo visibility; ran one throwaway SQLite probe in my scratch. PRE-MORTEM (the implementation shipped and failed; top ten, most likely first): (1) a v5 helper run from a worktree or the batch-3.5 probe migrates a live session DB, and the deployed v4 helper the hooks prefer then crashes on it (OBS-1); (2) the dotprofile copy runs before or without the export: two different SessionEnd hooks, a 1.5 s shared budget, export last after a network call (OBS-3); (3) dotprofile index.lock contention leaves copies uncommitted, and catch-up only recommits sessions/ (OBS-4); (4) session content keeps reaching the public repo through the tracked running-estimate.json and harvesting/ (OBS-5, OBS-6, OBS-7); (5) the per-turn estimate update has no table and no checklist line, so intent and assessment are never written (OBS-10); (6) one [s]kip in a deploy review menu splits hooks and bin across --session/--db (OBS-2); (7) the v4-to-v5 migration fails or drops data: NULL attributed_to, unmapped decisions, messages and finding columns (OBS-8), and intelligence-stop.py goes silently blind (OBS-9); (8) the AAR check never sees a background delegate's hand-back (OBS-14); (9) AAR item ids and refs break when the session agent records an AAR, and appended versions show up as duplicates (OBS-11, OBS-12); (10) the single implementing delegate runs out of context across ~20 batches, or waits forever on gate G1 (OBS-21). SECTION 4, strongest case for each rejected option: S-1 embedding the schemas in harness-db.py (as 3.6.8 does for the SQL) keeps one source; RFC choice still wins if the lookup path is specified. S-2 a Stop hook cannot write an assessment, but can detect a stale one; RFC choice wins only with that detection plus a store (OBS-10). S-3 one brief per workflow fan-out is heavy, but objectives differ per agent(); RFC wins. S-4 update-in-place plus a history table keeps provenance without forcing every reader to pick the latest version; the rejected option is at least as strong (OBS-12, PRO-12). S-5 columns per field make deviations by cause or objectives by status queryable; RFC 0010 section 11 does not mention JSON functions and json_extract works here; RFC choice acceptable, rationale weak (OBS-30). S-6 the rejected third-party validator is barred by RFC 0010; RFC wins, but the subset cannot enforce the spec's MUSTs (OBS-15). S-7 wins before schema 5; the remap after it is missing (OBS-11). S-8 a separate references or read_in_full node keeps binding rules apart from material under review; the rejected option wins (OBS-23). S-9 launching DB-writing delegates without isolation removes most of the fallback's holes; the rejected option should be the default (OBS-13). S-10 a spool file never loses a write, which exit 1 does unless the caller acts; RFC acceptable if it says what the caller does (OBS-20). S-11 the full id in the DB name is barred by D874d-48; RFC wins, the refusal needs a fallback (OBS-26). S-12 keeping the v4 tables untouched beside items avoids the view's write failure; RFC can win with a view contract and a version guard (OBS-1, OBS-9). S-13 keeping the old export during transition keeps the dashboard working, but it publishes session content; retire it earlier, not later (OBS-5, OBS-24). S-14 excluding every .json and prompt dump is broader and matches what is already published; the rejected option wins (OBS-6). S-15 a deprecated, ignored --session alias for one release survives deploy skew; the rejected option wins (OBS-2, R874d-a4-1). S-16 RFC wins. S-17 the mapping is incomplete; no rejected option, but the claim 'No v4 data is lost' fails (OBS-8). S-18 RFC wins; folded-in level-2 items need their own writer fields (OBS-13).

observations.text: S-10's retry is unsafe for hooks and does not cover the real contention point. A hook that writes a row (agent_type hook) could block up to 5 s plus three backoffs on the hot path. And every write command first runs ensure_schema, whose executescript of ~20 DDL statements takes the write lock, so parallel writers contend on DDL before any INSERT. The RFC does not say what the caller does after exit 1.

operational_learning.text: To find your own agentId as a background delegate, grep the parent transcript for '"agentId":"<id>","description":"<mission name>' (one grep -o call). It worked at once for this mission; the toolUseResult is written at launch ('status':'async_launched').

A recursive grep from the aitools repo root ('.') walks .claude/worktrees/* and their .scratch HOME copies and does not finish in 120 s. Search named top-level dirs (shared, .claude/rules, scripts, reference) only, and stop a background task you no longer need with TaskStop.

Before trusting a 'reuse the existing mechanism' design, read that mechanism's log: ait-harvest.log showed 60 git failures, most of them index.lock contention, which the code review alone would not have shown.
A throwaway SQLite DB in the delegate's scratch is enough to prove schema-compatibility failures (view vs table DDL) without touching a live session DB.

My read of the design, honestly: the document model (one schema, items, provenance, AAR as hand-back) is sound and I found little to attack there. The risk sits in the plumbing it reuses (SessionEnd timing, the dotprofile git path, deploy skew, the harvester), which has failed before and is where the plan is thinnest.

proposals.text: Make v4 and v5 helpers safe on each other's DBs, and keep the live DB on the deployed schema until deploy
proposals.what: RFC 3.6.7: add 'ensure_schema MUST check schema_version before any migration step and, on a DB newer than the helper, change nothing and exit 1 with a clear error on write verbs; every v4-shape check MUST test sqlite_master type = table, not table_info. SESSION_SCHEMA MUST drop the observations index once observations is a view.' Plan 3.1: add a test 'a v4 helper (git show origin/main:scripts/harness-db.py) opened on a v5 DB fails cleanly, never DROPs'. Plan 3.5: old 'a delegate in an isolated worktree writes the session DB' -> new 'a delegate in an isolated worktree writes a throwaway copy of a session DB (sqlite3 backup API); never the live DB'. Brief 874d-2 constraints: add 'Never run a branch's harness-db.py against a live session DB or harness DB in the main checkout; the deployed ~/.aitools/bin copy is the only one that touches them until the commander deploys'. Also ship a v4 point release first (WP-3 batch 3.0) that moves the newer-version check before migrate_v4, so every machine's deployed v4 helper refuses a v5 DB.
proposals.why: Probe: a v4 helper DROPs/INDEXes a view and raises; hooks prefer the deployed helper (OBS-1).
proposals.barrier_analysis: Prevention (spec + test) stops the v4 crash; the brief constraint removes the only planned path that migrates a live DB early.

proposals.text: Survive deploy skew of hooks and bin
proposals.what: RFC 3.6.9 (S-15): append 'For one release after schema 5 ships, harness-db.py MUST accept --session as a deprecated, ignored argument on every verb that had it, logging a warning, so a deployed hook of either version works with a deployed helper of either version. The hooks MUST pass --db only when the helper's --help lists it.' Open R874d-a4-1 before writing it (D874d-31 says drop it 'all together').
proposals.why: deploy-harness reviews bin and hooks separately; one [s]kip splits them (OBS-2).
proposals.barrier_analysis: Removes the failure for the skew window; detection (the warning) shows when it is safe to drop the alias.

proposals.text: One SessionEnd pipeline: export, then copy, then commit, all detached; catch-up re-exports
proposals.what: RFC 3.5.5: old 'The copy and the push MUST run detached' -> new 'The export, the copy and the push MUST run as one detached sequence started by harness-db-sessionend.sh, in that order (export first; the copy reads the export just written). ship and process-events MUST NOT run before the export in the synchronous part. The next session's catch-up (session-catchup.sh) MUST re-export, from the session DB, any session whose DB is newer than its export, and copy any export newer than its record.' Plan 4.3 files: add shared/hooks/harness-db-sessionend.sh; Verify: add 'with CLAUDE_CODE_SESSIONEND_HOOKS_TIMEOUT_MS unset, the hook returns in well under 1.5 s; a cancelled hook leaves a state the next catch-up completes'.
proposals.why: Two hooks with no ordering and a 1.5 s budget, with the export last (OBS-3).
proposals.barrier_analysis: Ordering inside one process removes the race; catch-up from the DB (the durable store) removes the dependence on SessionEnd finishing.

proposals.text: Fix the dotprofile git path before adding a second writer to it
proposals.what: Plan 4.3: add to Files 'scripts/ait-harvest.py: archive and the estimate copy take HarvestLock, waiting up to their deadline instead of skipping; commit_pending_archives commits sessions/ and running-estimates/; commit_and_push refuses (logs, keeps the commit) when the branch is not main; when the worktree is dirty, fetch and rebase only the commit just made (or push to a retry next start), never leave a commit unpushed without a warning in the next SessionStart output'. Verify: 'two archive processes and one estimate copy started together all commit; a remote one commit ahead is pulled and the push succeeds'. RFC 3.5.5: add 'A copy or push that fails MUST be reported in the next SessionStart output, not only in ait-harvest.log'.
proposals.why: 60 logged git failures, mostly index.lock contention; no recovery for running-estimates/ (OBS-4).
proposals.barrier_analysis: The lock prevents same-machine contention; the extended recovery and the SessionStart report detect what still fails.

proposals.text: Stop publishing the single export now, not in WP-5
proposals.what: Plan: move from batch 5.2 to a new batch 3.4 item: 'harness-db-sessionend.sh stops writing .aitools/channel/running-estimate.json; git rm --cached .aitools/channel/running-estimate.json; .gitignore gains .aitools/channel/running-estimate.json'. Keep the template retirement in 5.2. RFC 3.5.6: add 'This retirement ships with schema 5 (WP-3), before any richer item reaches the export.' If the commander agrees, do it even sooner as its own one-line PR (R874d-a4-4).
proposals.why: The file is tracked in a PUBLIC repo and was committed with session content on 2026-11-15 (OBS-5).

proposals.text: Widen S-14 and make the interim guard mechanical
proposals.what: RFC section 7: old 'It MUST treat *-brief.json and *-aar.json as ephemeral. Until it does, a harvested brief MUST NOT be committed.' -> new 'It MUST treat as ephemeral *-brief.json, *-aar.json, *brief*.md, *briefing*.json and any file whose name contains prompt or rfi. Until it does, .gitignore MUST list harvesting/*-brief.json, harvesting/*-aar.json, harvesting/*brief*, harvesting/*prompt*, harvesting/*rfi*.' Plan: move batch 4.4's .gitignore half into WP-1 as batch 1.0. Surface the already-published files to the commander (R874d-a4-4); rewriting public history is his call.

proposals.text: Protect every repo, not only aitools

Plan 3.4: add harness-db-sessionstart.sh (or scratch-init.sh) to Files, with a test in a temp repo.

proposals.text: Complete the v4-to-v5 mapping
proposals.what: RFC 3.6.7 table: add rows 'decisions rows -> items of type decision (decision_id kept as id, title -> text, description, implementation_evidence, decided_at, implemented_at -> fields)'; 'observations columns evidence, confidence, criteria, cause, effect, suggestion, refs, legacy_category -> fields (refs also -> refs rows)'; 'attributed_to NULL -> agent_id "unknown", agent_type session'; 'messages rows stay in messages; log keeps writing messages (SITREP/SPOTREP are not items)'. Old 'type finding | observation (D874d-28)' -> new 'type finding | observation, with fields.legacy_type finding (a stored v4 finding records what was seen and analysed, not something done; D874d-28 retires the type, replacedBy: deviation, for new items)'. proposals.text: Give the observations view a column contract and move intelligence-stop.py to items

proposals.text: Give S-2 a store and a carrier

proposals.text: Specify id remapping
proposals.what: RFC 3.2.4: add 'An item's document id (OBS-1) is kept as fields.doc_id. When an AAR's items are written to the DB, harness-db.py MUST map each document id to the DB id it assigns and rewrite every ref in the same AAR. An AAR assumption that verifies a brief assumption carries fields.brief_ref ("ASM-1" of <brief path>). Delegates number RFIs R<sid4>-<mission name>-<n> until the session agent records them as R<sid4>-<n>.' Add 'item import --aar <file>' to 3.6.10 to do the mapping.

proposals.text: Make S-4 implementable
proposals.what: RFC 3.6.3: old 'items id, type, ... created_at, updated_at, version' -> new 'items id, version, type, ... created_at (PRIMARY KEY (id, version); no updated_at)', and add 'Readers (export, aar, the observations view, list) MUST use the latest version of each id. refs point to an id, meaning its latest version. item update appends a version.' Add version to the common fields of 3.2.1 as OPTIONAL in documents (default 1). Alternative (the rejected option, at least as strong): update in place with an append-only item_history table written by a trigger.
proposals.why: No key, a contradicting column, and no read rule (OBS-12).
proposals.barrier_analysis: Prevention: a schema constraint makes a duplicate (id, version) impossible; a test checks readers return one row per id.

proposals.text: Default to non-isolated delegates and close the fallback's holes
proposals.what: RFC 3.3.8 (S-9): add first 'A delegating agent MUST NOT launch a delegate that writes briefs or DB rows with Agent isolation "worktree"; it uses git worktree add, which does not confine writes.' Then: '3.5.4 also reads a briefs table in the session DB, where every delegating agent records the absolute path of each brief it writes (fallback briefs included)'; '3.4.8: each delegating agent, at any level, records the items of the AARs it receives that were not written as rows; an AAR states provenance.rows_written true|false|partial'; 'S-18: items folded in from another AAR keep their own agent_id, agent_type, mission'. Brief 874d-2 access.writable: add the session scratch dir /Users/new-jose/repos/aitools/.scratch/session-dbd05b0c-2365-4159-9976-bc64a2af874d/ for its delegates' briefs.
proposals.why: Missions vanish from missions[], level-2 AARs are orphaned, rows duplicate (OBS-13).
proposals.barrier_analysis: Removes the common case that triggers the fallback; makes the rare case complete.

proposals.text: Put the AAR check where hand-backs are, and define the parse
proposals.what: Plan 4.2: old 'PostToolUse on Agent, or SubagentStop' -> new 'SubagentStop (reads the delegate's final hand-back from its transcript) or PreToolUse on SubagentHandback; probe both first and record which sees a background delegate's AAR; PostToolUse on Agent sees only async_launched'. RFC 3.4.1: add 'The AAR is the last fenced block whose opening line is exactly three backticks followed by json; text before it is ignored; inside JSON strings a run of three backticks MUST be written with the JSON escape for the backtick character (u0060).'
proposals.why: Background launches return before the AAR exists; fence parsing is undefined (OBS-14).
proposals.barrier_analysis: Detection that actually sees the artifact it checks.

proposals.text: Add semantic checks beside the schema subset
proposals.what: RFC 3.7.2: append 'type MAY be an array (e.g. ["string", "null"]); the subset adds pattern and const. validate MUST also run these Python checks the schema cannot express: quote present when source.kind is commander; an objective not accomplished cites a deviation; ids match their pattern; timestamps end in Z.' Plan 1.4: add a negative case for each.

proposals.barrier_analysis: Detection of the spec's MUSTs at validation time.

proposals.text: Test the dotprofile push against a local bare remote

proposals.text: Resolve the session DB by session id, not by cwd
proposals.what: RFC 2 Terminology: add '<repo>: the git toplevel of the directory the top-level session started in, as the SessionStart hook resolved it'. RFC 3.6.1: add 'The SessionStart hook MUST record the DB's absolute path in the session scratch dir (.session-db) and in ~/.aitools/sessions-index (session id -> DB path); every later hook and the SessionEnd export resolve the DB from it, never from the current cwd.'
proposals.why: A cd into a worktree or another repo loses the export (OBS-17).
proposals.barrier_analysis: Prevention: one resolution recorded at start.

proposals.text: Define <project> and the date of the record
proposals.what: RFC 3.8 Record row: add '<project>: the basename of the main worktree of <repo> (git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir, parent dir name), so a worktree session files under its project; <YYYY-MM-DD>: the UTC date of session.started_at (stable across resume and midnight; the example 2026-11-15_dbd05b0c-2.json)'. Confirm with R874d-a4-2.

proposals.barrier_analysis: Prevention: one deterministic name per session.

proposals.text: Scope the --session removal
proposals.what: RFC 3.6.9: old '--session MUST be removed' -> new '--session MUST be removed from every verb that writes or reads the session DB (they take --db). proposals.text: Bound the retry for hooks and move schema work out of the write path
proposals.what: RFC 3.6.6: append 'Hooks pass --no-retry with busy_timeout 200 and on failure append the item to <session scratch>/pending-items.jsonl, which the next successful write (or SessionEnd export) drains. ensure_schema runs only when schema_version is below the helper's, not on every write. After exit 1, an agent records the item in its AAR and says it was not written.'
proposals.why: Hot-path budget and DDL contention (OBS-20).
proposals.barrier_analysis: Prevention of hook stalls; no lost write.

proposals.text: Make the implementing mission an orchestrator and fix the gates
proposals.what: Brief 874d-2 duties: add 'You are an orchestrator: one fresh delegate per batch (two or three files), each with its own brief; you verify between batches and own the PRs.' proposals.text: List D-DEL13 as a point the RFC settles, and keep the standing duties in the prompt until deploy

proposals.text: Correct two brief items
proposals.what: Brief 874d-2 ASM-6: status 'verified' -> 'unverified', evidence '36 bits' -> '36 bits makes a collision unlikely; checked at session start (RFC 0011 3.6.2)'. OL-2: old '... was created when the delegate finished (20:55:18Z), not at launch; do not rely on it while a delegate runs' -> new 'was created at launch for 874d-4-adversarial (2026-11-16) but at finish for 874d-1-aar-doctrine; do not rely on it while a delegate runs; the parent transcript's toolUseResult (agentId, description) is written at launch'.
proposals.why: OBS-29.
proposals.barrier_analysis: Keeps the brief's intelligence honest.

proposals.text: Fix S-5's rationale
proposals.what: RFC 3.6.4 / S-5 Why: old 'Python 3.8 does not guarantee SQLite's JSON functions (RFC 0010 section 11)' -> new 'The JSON1 functions are built into SQLite only from 3.38.0; the SQLite version bundled with a Python 3.8 build is not fixed, so the harness does not rely on them (RFC 0010 section 2, stdlib portability)'. Whether 3.38.0 is the right number: verify on sqlite.org with the browser before writing it.
proposals.why: The cited section does not say it (OBS-30).
proposals.barrier_analysis: Accurate provenance.

proposals.text: Say where the status table is updated
proposals.what: Plan 'How every batch is shipped': old 'After each batch, update the status table at the end of this plan.' -> new 'After each batch, update the status table on main under the Channel exception (git pull --ff-only, commit only plans/structured-reports/implementation-plan.md, push), never on a feature branch.' Brief 874d-2 access.writable: add that file for direct-to-main commits.
proposals.why: OBS-31.
proposals.barrier_analysis: Prevents merge conflicts on the plan.

proposals.text: Clarify 'no session-id column'
proposals.what: RFC 3.6.3: old 'There is no session-id column (D874d-31): the file is the session, and the export adds the id.' -> new 'items and refs have no session-id column (D874d-31): the file is the session. The session table keeps the full session id (one row), which the export and 3.6.2 read.'
proposals.why: OBS-32.
proposals.barrier_analysis: Prevention of a destructive misreading.

rfis.title: May harness-db.py keep --session as a deprecated, ignored alias for one release?
rfis.question: D874d-31: 'we can drop that column and argument all together'. deploy-harness reviews ~/.aitools/bin/harness-db.py and the hooks separately, so one [s]kip pairs a new hook with an old helper or the reverse, and the hooks fail silently (OBS-2). A one-release alias that is accepted and ignored, with a warning, covers that window. Is that within your decision, or do you want --session gone in the same release?
rfis.suggestion: Allow the alias for one release, removed in the release after WP-6 (PRO-2), because it is the only barrier against skew that does not depend on how you answer a deploy menu.

rfis.title: Which date and project name does the dotprofile record use?
rfis.question: You agreed to running-estimates/<project>/<YYYY-MM-DD>_<session id prefix>.json, 'laid out like the session archives', with the example 2026-11-15_dbd05b0c-2.json (L2439, L2442). The archives use the transcript's last-modified date and the git-root name, which would name this session's record 2026-11-16_... and a worktree session under the worktree's name (OBS-18).
rfis.suggestion: The session's start date (UTC) and the main repo's name, as in your example (PRO-18), so a resumed session overwrites one file instead of creating a second.

rfis.title: What did '27) dont worry about it' mean for the six uncommitted files?
rfis.question: R874d-27 suggested the session agent commit the six working-copy files on a branch with a PR. The plan reads your answer as 'the commander takes care of this' and blocks WP-1 and WP-2 on it (gate G1). WP-1 does not touch those files (OBS-21).
rfis.suggestion: WP-1 starts without G1; WP-2 waits for G1 and raises an RFI if it is still open then (PRO-21).

rfis.title: Untrack the single running-estimate export and block harvested briefs, AARs and prompt dumps now?
rfis.question: nobul-tech/aitools is public. .aitools/channel/running-estimate.json is tracked and was committed on 2026-11-15 with session content; tracked harvesting/ already holds AARs, briefs and dumps of your prompts (OBS-5, OBS-6). The plan retires the export only in WP-5.
rfis.suggestion: One small PR now: git rm --cached the export, add it and the harvesting patterns of PRO-6 to .gitignore. Leave the already-published files and history as they are unless you order a history rewrite, which is destructive and yours to decide.

rfis.title: May the harness add .aitools/ and .scratch/ to .git/info/exclude in every repo it runs in?
rfis.question: In repos other than aitools nothing ignores them, so the per-session export and every brief are one 'git add -A' away from a commit (OBS-7). info/exclude is local to the clone and never committed.
rfis.suggestion: Yes, at SessionStart, reported once per repo (PRO-7).
